sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: Mobile phones have undergone a profound transformation from basic communication devices into powerful digital ecosystems. They now mediate social interaction, financial transactions, education, entertainment, and access to information. Rapid technological innovation has shortened product life cycles, encouraging frequent replacement of devices. This culture of constant upgrading reinforces consumer dependency and contributes significantly to electronic waste. Algorithm-driven applications shape user behavior by controlling attention through notifications and personalized content. While such features enhance convenience and efficiency, they also reduce uninterrupted concentration and deepen psychological reliance. Mobile phones increasingly blur boundaries between work and personal life. Although digital connectivity expands opportunities, it simultaneously raises concerns about autonomy and informed choice. The challenge lies not in rejecting technology but in regulating its influence on human behavior and decision-making.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Garment technology in India has evolved rapidly due to the intersection of traditional textile expertise and modern industrial innovation. Automation, computer-aided design, and advanced sewing machinery have increased production efficiency and precision, while preserving the aesthetic complexity of indigenous fabrics. The sector faces challenges in maintaining quality amidst mass production, as well as in integrating sustainable practices in dyeing, weaving, and waste management. Global competition compels manufacturers to adopt fast fashion techniques without compromising ethical labor standards. Research in smart textiles, wearable electronics, and fabric durability is gradually transforming India into a hub for high-value apparel. Workforce skill development remains critical, as technological sophistication requires trained operators. Consequently, garment technology in India exemplifies the tension between preserving heritage, embracing innovation, and meeting global market demands.

questions.q: Identify the error: “She is having three older brothers who live in Delhi.”
questions.why: 'Have' meaning possession is not used in the continuous: 'She has'. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “He was angry ____ the unfair decision.”
questions.why: Angry at a thing (angry with a person). GPSC CBRT, May 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “They expect her to complete the task soon.”
opts: She is expected to complete the task soon.
She expected to complete the task soon.
She is expected completing the task soon.
It is expected her to complete the task soon.
questions.why: Present 'expect' becomes 'is expected', infinitive kept. GPSC CBRT, May 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “By next month, she ____ here for ten years.”
questions.why: 'By' + future time takes the future perfect. GPSC CBRT, May 2026.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “lethargic”:
questions.why: Lethargic means lacking energy. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The Chhattisgarh Cabinet approved ₹500 crore in September 2026 for the:
The GST Council, whose 57th meeting was held in October 2026, is constituted under Article:
questions.why: Added by the 101st Amendment, 2016.

questions.q: Pune will host the 2032 UCI Road World Championships in:
questions.why: UCI is the world governing body for cycling. Oct 2026.

questions.q: Glasgow, host of the 2026 Commonwealth Games, is in:
questions.why: Ahmedabad hosts the 2030 Games, India's second after Delhi 2010.

questions.q: Engineers' Day (15 September) is observed on the birth anniversary of:
questions.why: Static.

questions.q: How many Lok Sabha seats does Goa have?
questions.why: North Goa and South Goa. Goa has 40 assembly seats and 1 Rajya Sabha seat.

questions.q: India's retail (CPI) inflation for September 2026 was:
questions.why: Up from 4.82% in August. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The third International Bharat 6G Symposium (2026) was held alongside the:
Sethuraman Panchanathan, named for the 2026 Arthur M. Bueche Award, is a:
questions.why: Given by the US National Academy of Engineering. Sep 2026.

questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in:
questions.why: In Amritsar, on 13 April.

questions.q: Gauri bought things worth ₹25, of which 30 paise was sales tax at 6% on taxable items. What was the cost of the tax-free items?
questions.why: Taxable items: 0.30 ÷ 0.06 = ₹5. Tax-free = 25 − 5 − 0.30 = ₹19.70. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.

questions.q: From a point P on level ground, the top of a 100 m tower is at an elevation of 30°. How far is P from the foot of the tower?
What is the profit per cent on an article? I. 5% discount is given on the list price. II. Without the discount, the profit would be 20%. III. The cost price is ₹5,000. Which statements are necessary?
questions.why: List = 1.2 × cost, sold at 0.95 × list = 1.14 × cost: 14% profit. The cost figure isn't needed. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: The present ages of Sameer and Anand are in the ratio 5 : 4. Three years hence it will be 11 : 9. What is Anand's present age?
questions.why: 9(5x + 3) = 11(4x + 3), so x = 6 and Anand = 24. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: If P means +, Q means −, R means × and S means ÷, what is 8 R 2 S 4 Q 6 P 2?
What is the next number? 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, …
questions.why: Consecutive primes: next is 19. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which does not belong? Jurisprudence, Criminology, Penology, Entomology
questions.why: Entomology is the study of insects; the rest concern law and crime. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: If BEAUTY is coded as DHEZZF, how is FLOWER written?
questions.why: Shifts +2, +3, +4, +5, +6, +7 (wrapping round): F→H, L→O, O→S, W→B, E→K, R→Y. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Find the wrong number: 12, 25, 49, 99, 187, 395, 789
questions.why: × 2 + 1, × 2 − 1 by turns: 99 × 2 − 1 = 197, not 187. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Rohan is 21st from the top and 15th from the bottom of his class. How many students are there?
The palliative method that treats with an opposite (contraria contrariis) is called:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Hahnemann discussed it in §§57–60; relief is followed by worsening.

questions.q: Hahnemann regarded a local disease on the outer parts of the body (§185 onward) as:
opts: purely local, to be treated by external applications
an expression of an internal disease of the whole organism
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. He treated such conditions internally.

questions.q: Kent's second observation, a long aggravation followed by slow final improvement, suggests:
opts: marked tissue changes, though the patient may recover slowly
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The vital force reacts with difficulty because of organic change.

questions.q: A haughty, proud woman who looks down on others, with numbness and over-sensitive genitals, calls for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Platina's pride and contempt.

questions.q: Weakness with trembling, desire for open air, craving for salt and sugar, and an aggravation from warmth suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Argentum nitricum: warm-blooded, hurried, craving sweets.

questions.q: Hoarseness and loss of voice with a raw, sore larynx; paralytic weakness and sympathy for others' suffering suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Causticum: paralytic weakness, deep sympathy, hoarseness worse mornings.

questions.q: A remedy for alcoholic or cardiac weakness with a slow, irregular pulse and a feeling that the heart will stop if he moves is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Digitalis: very slow pulse, fears the heart will stop if he moves (contrast Gelsemium).

questions.q: In the decimal scale, the first potency (1X) has a drug-to-vehicle ratio of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. One part drug to nine parts vehicle.

questions.q: The Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of India is published by:
opts: the Government of India (Ministry of AYUSH, through the Pharmacopoeia Commission)
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Now prepared by the Pharmacopoeia Commission for Indian Medicine and Homoeopathy.

questions.q: The process of choosing the most similar remedy using a repertory is called:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. It narrows the remedies to a few for study in the materia medica.

questions.q: Barthel and Klunker's 'Synthetic Repertory' covers mainly:
opts: Mind, Generalities, and Sleep, Dreams and Sexuality
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Three volumes of general symptoms.

questions.q: The 'carrying angle' is formed at the:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Between the long axes of the arm and forearm in extension.

questions.q: The cardiac output equals:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. About 5 L/min at rest.

questions.q: Change of one type of differentiated epithelium into another, as in a smoker's bronchus, is called:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Columnar to squamous metaplasia.

questions.q: Rice-water stools with severe dehydration are characteristic of:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Vibrio cholerae.

questions.q: Fever, pain in the right hypochondrium and arrest of inspiration on palpation under the right costal margin (Murphy's sign) suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Murphy's sign is the classic sign of acute cholecystitis.

questions.q: Chronic cough with fever, night sweats, weight loss and haemoptysis most suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Test sputum for TB.

questions.q: An itching, moist eczema behind the ears oozing a sticky, honey-like fluid suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Graphites: honey-like discharge, cracks in folds.

questions.q: The commonest site of ectopic pregnancy is the:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Tubal pregnancies are most often ampullary.

questions.q: A child says the first one or two meaningful words (such as 'mama') at about:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Two-word sentences by about 2 years.

questions.q: A pathological communication between two epithelial surfaces is called a:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. A sinus is a blind tract.

questions.q: Pain and tenderness in the right iliac fossa at McBurney's point suggest:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. One-third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.

questions.q: The infant mortality rate is the number of deaths of infants under one year per:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. A sensitive indicator of community health.

questions.q: Pin-point pupils, excessive salivation and sweating, muscle fasciculations and a kerosene-like smell suggest poisoning by:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Cholinergic crisis; serum cholinesterase is low. Datura dilates the pupils.

questions.q: A registered medical practitioner who fails to exercise reasonable skill and care, causing harm, may be liable for:
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Duty, breach, damage and causation.
